newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moslems rebels kill 22 in Algerian village.
newsitem.headline: Moslems rebels kill 22 in Algerian village.

text.p: Moslem rebels killed 22 people in Algeria by cutting their throats during an overnight raid on Menaa village, south of the capital Algiers, security forces said on Saturday.
A statement read on state-run radio said the 22 were "assassinated in a cowardly way", the official term used for rebels committing murders by cutting throats.
It said the massacre occurred overnight in Menaa hamlet, near Bouafrik, 30 km (18 miles) south of Algiers.
It blamed Moslem guerrillas for the killings but gave no further details.
The killing brought to about 140 the number of people slaughtered in a wave of renewed massacres during the past week.

Over the past seven days, Moslem guerrillas have massacred nearly 120 people, mostly villagers in remote areas, killing some with chainsaws, dousing others in burning petrol or shooting them dead at point blank range in several regions across the country, according to Algerian newspapers.
In the worst attack in five years of violence in Algeria, Moslem rebels exterminated all the 52 inhabitants of a village in Medea province, 70 km (45 miles) south of Algiers, last week.
Algeria is gearing up for June 5 legislative elections in which more than 30 political parties will take part.
The outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) called on Algerians to boycott the poll which it said would be neither free nor fair.
Algeria has been without an elected parliament since January 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which FIS had taken a huge lead.
About 60,000 people have died in the North African country's five-year old violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces.
